subjects.subject: Python & Coding Logic
subjects.overview: Master Python programming fundamentals, dynamic typing, control flow, functions, OOP, and file handling for placement coding rounds.

rag_chunks.subject: Python & Coding Logic
rag_chunks.definition: In Python, variables are names referencing objects in memory. Types belong to objects, not variable names.
rag_chunks.formula_or_core_rule: Mutable: list, dict, set (in-place modification allowed). Immutable: int, float, str, tuple (hashable, state cannot change).
rag_chunks.worked_example: a = [1]; b = a; b.append(2) results in a == [1, 2] because both labels reference the same heap object.
rag_chunks.content: Variables in Python store object references. Equality '==' checks values, whereas identity 'is' verifies memory addresses. Immutable types can safely act as dictionary keys.

rag_chunks.subject: Python & Coding Logic
rag_chunks.definition: Python uses pass-by-object-reference. Functions share references with callers; default arguments are evaluated only once at definition time.
rag_chunks.formula_or_core_rule: Never use def f(x=[]); always use def f(x=None): if x is None: x = [] to avoid retaining state across function calls.
rag_chunks.worked_example: def add(x, l=[]): l.append(x); return l. Multiple calls accumulate items because the list object persists across invocations.
rag_chunks.content: A high-frequency placement question: default arguments retain their state across successive calls if initialized with mutable types like lists or dictionaries.

rag_chunks.subject: Python & Coding Logic
rag_chunks.definition: Comprehensions are concise syntactic constructs in Python to create lists, sets, or dictionaries by applying expressions over an iterable.
rag_chunks.formula_or_core_rule: [expr for item in iterable if condition]; {k: v for item in iterable if condition}.
rag_chunks.worked_example: evens = [x for x in range(10) if x % 2 == 0] produces [0, 2, 4, 6, 8] cleanly in one line.
rag_chunks.content: Comprehensions are faster than traditional append loops because the byte-code loop runs in C-speed without repeated lookup of list.append.

rag_chunks.subject: Python & Coding Logic
rag_chunks.definition: The 'for...else' construct executes when no break occurs. Generator expressions produce values lazily using minimal memory.
rag_chunks.formula_or_core_rule: Use (x for x in seq) for large streams; use for...else to eliminate boolean search flags.
rag_chunks.worked_example: for n in [2, 4, 6]: if n == 5: break; else: print('No odd number found') executes the else branch.
rag_chunks.content: Placement rounds evaluate code elegance. Knowing loop-else and generator expressions demonstrates senior Python fluency.

rag_chunks.subject: Python & Coding Logic
rag_chunks.definition: Python resolves names using the LEGB hierarchy. A closure is a nested function that retains access to variables from its lexical enclosing scope.
rag_chunks.formula_or_core_rule: Local -> Enclosing -> Global -> Built-in. Use 'nonlocal' to modify enclosing variables in closures.
rag_chunks.worked_example: def outer(x): def inner(): return x + 1; return inner. Calling outer(5)() returns 6 because 'x' is enclosed.
rag_chunks.content: Understanding closures and scope resolution is crucial for coding rounds involving function factories and state encapsulation without classes.

rag_chunks.subject: Python & Coding Logic
rag_chunks.definition: Decorators wrap functions to dynamically inject logging, timing, authentication, or caching logic without changing the original code.
rag_chunks.formula_or_core_rule: def deco(f): def wrapper(*args, **kw): return f(*args, **kw); return wrapper.
rag_chunks.worked_example: @lru_cache(maxsize=None) caches expensive recursive Fibonacci calculations from exponential O(2^N) to linear O(N).
rag_chunks.content: Decorators are standard practice in production code (FastAPI, Flask, Django). Interviewers assess familiarity with functools.wraps and wrappers.

rag_chunks.subject: Python & Coding Logic
rag_chunks.definition: OOP organizes software into classes bundling state and behaviors. Dunder methods hook into Python operators and built-in functions.
rag_chunks.formula_or_core_rule: __repr__ for debugging, __str__ for human display, __eq__ for value comparison, __len__ for sizing.
rag_chunks.worked_example: class Point: def __init__(self, x, y): self.x, self.y = x, y. Implementing __repr__ returns f'Point({self.x}, {self.y})'.
rag_chunks.content: Encapsulation in Python relies on naming conventions: single underscore for protected internal use, double underscore for name mangled private attributes.

rag_chunks.subject: Python & Coding Logic
rag_chunks.definition: Polymorphism allows different subclasses to share a unified method signature with customized implementations.
rag_chunks.formula_or_core_rule: Class.mro() outlines resolution order. Use super().__init__() to invoke parent initializers correctly.
rag_chunks.worked_example: In multiple inheritance (class C(A, B)), C.__mro__ determines which implementation executes first when calling super().
rag_chunks.content: Placement technical rounds frequently assess the difference between instance methods (self), class methods (cls), and static methods (@staticmethod).

rag_chunks.subject: Python & Coding Logic
rag_chunks.definition: Exception handling intercepts runtime anomalies, allowing graceful recovery or structured resource teardown.
rag_chunks.formula_or_core_rule: Catch specific exceptions. Reserve 'finally' for cleanup. Use custom exceptions inheriting from Exception.
rag_chunks.worked_example: class InsufficientFundsError(Exception): pass. Raising domain-specific errors improves API clarity and debuggability.
rag_chunks.content: Interviewers check whether candidates catch specific exceptions rather than using broad catch-all statements that mask bugs.

rag_chunks.subject: Python & Coding Logic
rag_chunks.definition: Context managers guarantee deterministic resource acquisition and release using the 'with' statement.
rag_chunks.formula_or_core_rule: with open('f.txt', 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f: process(f). Always specify encoding explicitly.
rag_chunks.worked_example: from contextlib import contextmanager; @contextmanager def tag(name): print(f'<{name}>'); yield; print(f'</{name}>').
rag_chunks.content: Using context managers prevents socket and file descriptor leaks in production microservices and high-throughput servers.

subjects.subject: SQL & Database Management
subjects.overview: Master relational database schema design, keys, joins, aggregation, normalization (1NF-3NF), ACID transactions, and indexing.
topics: Basic SELECT, WHERE, GROUP BY & HAVING
JOIN Operations (INNER, LEFT, RIGHT, FULL OUTER)

rag_chunks.subject: SQL & Database Management
rag_chunks.definition: Relational keys guarantee entity integrity and referential integrity across interconnected relational tables.
rag_chunks.formula_or_core_rule: Primary Key: 1 per table, NOT NULL + UNIQUE. Foreign Key: enforces parent-child relational integrity.
rag_chunks.worked_example: In an e-commerce schema, Orders.customer_id is a Foreign Key referencing Customers.id, preventing orphan orders.
rag_chunks.content: Mastering the distinctions between Primary, Candidate, Super, and Foreign Keys is a staple of placement rounds for software engineering roles.

rag_chunks.subject: SQL & Database Management
rag_chunks.definition: Referential actions determine how updates and deletions in parent tables propagate to associated child rows.
rag_chunks.formula_or_core_rule: TRUNCATE deallocates pages (DDL, faster). DELETE logs row-by-row (DML, can be filtered with WHERE).
rag_chunks.worked_example: ON DELETE RESTRICT prevents accidental deletion of departments that currently have active assigned employees.
rag_chunks.content: Interviewers frequently ask candidates to explain the differences between DROP, TRUNCATE, and DELETE in terms of transactions, rollbacks, and triggers.

rag_chunks.subject: SQL & Database Management
rag_chunks.chapter: Basic SELECT, WHERE, GROUP BY & HAVING
rag_chunks.definition: SQL statements are evaluated in a strict logical order: FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, SELECT, ORDER BY, LIMIT.
rag_chunks.formula_or_core_rule: F-W-G-H-S-O-L. Column aliases created in SELECT cannot be filtered in WHERE.
rag_chunks.worked_example: WHERE filters base records prior to aggregation; HAVING filters aggregated metrics produced by GROUP BY.
rag_chunks.content: This order explains why aliases declared in SELECT are unavailable in WHERE, but are legal in ORDER BY.

rag_chunks.subject: SQL & Database Management
rag_chunks.chapter: Basic SELECT, WHERE, GROUP BY & HAVING
rag_chunks.definition: Aggregate functions compute summary values across grouped records, ignoring NULLs in column expressions.
rag_chunks.formula_or_core_rule: COUNT(*) counts rows; COUNT(col) ignores NULL. UNION deduplicates; UNION ALL preserves duplicates.
rag_chunks.worked_example: AVG(score) calculates SUM(score) / COUNT(score), effectively ignoring students who did not sit for the exam.
rag_chunks.content: Understanding how NULLs distort aggregate averages is a high-yield topic tested in technical database screenings.

rag_chunks.subject: SQL & Database Management
rag_chunks.chapter: JOIN Operations (INNER, LEFT, RIGHT, FULL OUTER)
rag_chunks.definition: JOIN operations combine columns from two or more tables based on related matching key attributes.
rag_chunks.formula_or_core_rule: INNER: mutual match. LEFT: all left + matched right. Anti-join: LEFT JOIN ... WHERE right.id IS NULL.
rag_chunks.worked_example: Finding users without orders: SELECT u.id FROM users u LEFT JOIN orders o ON u.id = o.user_id WHERE o.id IS NULL.
rag_chunks.content: Outer joins and anti-join patterns are essential for database query questions in FAANG and tier-1 product technical rounds.

rag_chunks.subject: SQL & Database Management
rag_chunks.chapter: JOIN Operations (INNER, LEFT, RIGHT, FULL OUTER)
rag_chunks.topic: Self Joins, Cross Joins & Cartesian Products
rag_chunks.definition: A self join models recursive relationships within a single table. A cross join generates all combinations across tables.
rag_chunks.formula_or_core_rule: Self join requires aliases: FROM emp e LEFT JOIN emp m ON e.mgr_id = m.id. Cross join row count = M * N.
rag_chunks.worked_example: Pairwise comparisons or employee-manager trees require self-joins to correlate rows within the same physical entity.
rag_chunks.content: Interviewers check whether candidates understand the exponential performance risks of unintended cross joins in large data sets.

rag_chunks.subject: SQL & Database Management
rag_chunks.definition: Normalization systematically decomposes relations to minimize data redundancy and prevent insertion, update, and deletion anomalies.
rag_chunks.formula_or_core_rule: 1NF: atomic values. 2NF: no partial dependencies where an attribute depends on only part of a composite key.
rag_chunks.worked_example: Splitting a table with (StudentID, CourseID) -> CourseFee into separate tables ensures fee updates occur in exactly one place.
rag_chunks.content: Understanding normalization anomalies is a core requirement in relational database design and campus placement interviews.

rag_chunks.subject: SQL & Database Management
rag_chunks.definition: 3NF removes transitive dependencies (non-key determining non-key). BCNF enforces that every determinant is a superkey.
rag_chunks.formula_or_core_rule: 3NF eliminates A -> B -> C. Denormalize in OLAP to trade storage for query speed by pre-joining tables.
rag_chunks.worked_example: Separating ZipCode -> City from Employee address details satisfies 3NF by isolating transitive dependencies.
rag_chunks.content: Senior candidates are expected to articulate when to normalize (OLTP) versus when to denormalize (OLAP/Star Schema).

rag_chunks.subject: SQL & Database Management
rag_chunks.definition: ACID properties govern database transaction reliability. Isolation levels balance concurrency against data consistency anomalies.
rag_chunks.formula_or_core_rule: Atomicity (all-or-nothing), Durability (WAL logs). Isolation levels: Read Uncommitted < Read Committed < Repeatable Read < Serializable.
rag_chunks.worked_example: Repeatable Read prevents rows from altering during a transaction, but Serializable is required to eliminate phantom inserts.
rag_chunks.content: Transaction mechanics and concurrency isolation levels are prime discussion points in systems engineering and database interviews.

rag_chunks.subject: SQL & Database Management
rag_chunks.topic: Indexing Strategies: Clustered vs Non-Clustered & B-Trees
rag_chunks.definition: Database indexes are auxiliary data structures (typically B-Trees) that accelerate row retrieval at the cost of slower write throughput.
rag_chunks.formula_or_core_rule: Clustered index (1 per table, orders physical rows). Non-clustered (multiple, stores pointers to data pages).
rag_chunks.worked_example: Adding an index on employee.email reduces query time from 2.5s (full scan) to 2ms (B-Tree index seek).
rag_chunks.content: Candidates must understand the trade-offs of indexing: speeding up selective queries versus degrading high-volume batch writes.

subjects.subject: AI & Modern Tech Concepts
subjects.overview: Understand modern GenAI, LLMs, prompt engineering, RAG, REST APIs, cloud computing (IaaS/PaaS/SaaS), and web cybersecurity.
topics: REST APIs, HTTP Verbs & JSON Communication
Cloud Computing Basics (IaaS vs PaaS vs SaaS)

rag_chunks.subject: AI & Modern Tech Concepts
rag_chunks.definition: Large Language Models are autoregressive neural networks trained to predict the next token across extensive text distributions.
rag_chunks.formula_or_core_rule: 1 token ≈ 4 characters (0.75 words). Text is split into subword tokens via BPE before embedding lookup.
rag_chunks.worked_example: The word 'unbelievable' may tokenize into ['un', 'believ', 'able'], allowing models to generalize across shared root words.
rag_chunks.content: Understanding token limits, vocabulary construction, and context windows is essential for GenAI application architecture.

rag_chunks.subject: AI & Modern Tech Concepts
rag_chunks.definition: Inference parameters control the randomness and breadth of candidate token selection during text generation.
rag_chunks.formula_or_core_rule: Low temp (0.0 - 0.2) for deterministic code/math; high temp (0.7 - 1.0) for creative tasks. Top-P caps cumulative distribution.
rag_chunks.worked_example: Setting temperature=0.1 in an automated SQL code generator guarantees reproducible, syntactically correct queries.
rag_chunks.content: Interviewers frequently evaluate whether candidates understand how temperature and nucleus sampling influence hallucination and output stability.

rag_chunks.subject: AI & Modern Tech Concepts
rag_chunks.definition: Prompt engineering optimizes instructions provided to foundation models to elicit accurate, structured, and consistent completions.
rag_chunks.formula_or_core_rule: Zero-shot (direct instruction). Few-shot (in-context exemplars). Chain-of-Thought (step-by-step reasoning decomposition).
rag_chunks.worked_example: Asking an LLM 'Let\'s solve this step by step' increases accuracy on multi-step arithmetic benchmarks from 17% to 78%.
rag_chunks.content: Designing effective prompts is a standard interview competency across GenAI developer and solutions engineering roles.

rag_chunks.subject: AI & Modern Tech Concepts
rag_chunks.definition: RAG combines vector search over embedded enterprise documents with LLM generation to eliminate hallucinations and outdated cutoffs.
rag_chunks.formula_or_core_rule: Cosine Similarity: (A · B) / (||A|| ||B||). Split -> Embed -> Index -> Retrieve -> Augment -> Generate.
rag_chunks.worked_example: A technical support bot retrieves the exact product firmware manual page to diagnose an error code accurately.
rag_chunks.content: Interviewers frequently ask candidates to diagram a complete end-to-end RAG architecture with vector databases and rerankers.

rag_chunks.subject: AI & Modern Tech Concepts
rag_chunks.chapter: REST APIs, HTTP Verbs & JSON Communication
rag_chunks.definition: REST is an architectural style for distributed systems utilizing stateless, uniform HTTP methods for CRUD operations.
rag_chunks.formula_or_core_rule: Idempotent verbs: GET, PUT, DELETE. Non-idempotent: POST. Use nouns for URI endpoints, verbs for actions.
rag_chunks.worked_example: PUT /users/42 replaces user 42 completely; PATCH /users/42 with {'email': 'new@mail.com'} updates only the email field.
rag_chunks.content: Designing clean REST endpoints and understanding idempotency is an essential interview skill in full-stack and backend software engineering.

rag_chunks.subject: AI & Modern Tech Concepts
rag_chunks.chapter: REST APIs, HTTP Verbs & JSON Communication
rag_chunks.definition: HTTP status codes communicate the execution outcome of client API requests across standardized category ranges.
rag_chunks.formula_or_core_rule: 2xx success, 3xx redirect, 4xx client error (401 unauthenticated vs 403 forbidden), 5xx server error.
rag_chunks.worked_example: Returning 201 Created with a Location header upon successful resource creation provides client guidance.
rag_chunks.content: Candidates must clearly explain how clients and servers exchange JSON payloads, handle authentication headers, and interpret error codes.

rag_chunks.subject: AI & Modern Tech Concepts
rag_chunks.chapter: Cloud Computing Basics (IaaS vs PaaS vs SaaS)
rag_chunks.definition: Cloud computing provides on-demand computing resources over the internet on a pay-as-you-go pricing model.
rag_chunks.formula_or_core_rule: IaaS (virtual hardware). PaaS (managed runtime/code). SaaS (end-user software). Customer always owns data security.
rag_chunks.worked_example: Hosting code on AWS Elastic Beanstalk (PaaS) frees engineering teams from patching Linux kernels or provisioning hypervisors.
rag_chunks.content: Understanding where provider obligations end and customer responsibilities begin is a foundational cloud interview question.

rag_chunks.subject: AI & Modern Tech Concepts
rag_chunks.chapter: Cloud Computing Basics (IaaS vs PaaS vs SaaS)
rag_chunks.definition: Horizontal scaling distributes incoming network traffic across redundant server instances to guarantee fault tolerance.
rag_chunks.formula_or_core_rule: Scale out over scale up: avoids single points of failure and hardware ceilings. Multi-AZ protects against facility outages.
rag_chunks.worked_example: An auto-scaling group scales from 2 to 20 instances during peak festival sales, scaling back down when load subsides.
rag_chunks.content: System design rounds for campus placements test ability to architect resilient, cost-effective cloud application tiers.

rag_chunks.subject: AI & Modern Tech Concepts
rag_chunks.definition: HTTPS secures web communication over TLS by establishing identity via asymmetric certificates and encrypting traffic with fast symmetric ciphers.
rag_chunks.formula_or_core_rule: Asymmetric (Public/Private key) for handshake key exchange; Symmetric (AES) for high-speed session data transmission.
rag_chunks.worked_example: Browser verifies server certificate with a trusted Certificate Authority (CA) before sending encrypted symmetric session keys.
rag_chunks.content: Understanding the TLS handshake and encryption mechanics is a standard security evaluation topic in engineering placements.

rag_chunks.subject: AI & Modern Tech Concepts
rag_chunks.definition: Web security relies on salted one-way password hashing (bcrypt) and signed claims (JWT) alongside parameterized database queries.
rag_chunks.formula_or_core_rule: Never encrypt passwords; hash with bcrypt + salt. Prevent SQLi using prepared statements. Sanitize inputs to prevent XSS.
rag_chunks.worked_example: JWT Header specifies alg, Payload holds user claims, and Signature verifies tampering without needing database queries on every call.
rag_chunks.content: Interviewers scrutinize candidates on password storage security, JWT mechanics, and OWASP Top 10 mitigation strategies.

subjects.subject: Aptitude & Interview Prep
subjects.overview: Master quantitative problem solving, logical series, speed-work formulas, behavioral STAR interview answers, and impactful resume building.
topics: Verbal & HR: The STAR Method for Behavioral Interviews
Technical Resume Building: Action Verbs & Impact Metrics

rag_chunks.subject: Aptitude & Interview Prep
rag_chunks.definition: Percentages scale comparisons to base-100 proportions. Multipliers eliminate multi-step arithmetic in competitive exams.
rag_chunks.formula_or_core_rule: Successive net change = a + b + (ab / 100). Fraction conversions: 1/6 = 16.67%, 1/8 = 12.5%.
rag_chunks.worked_example: A price rising 25% then falling 20% returns to 1.25 * 0.80 = 1.00 (original baseline price).
rag_chunks.content: Mastering mental percentage conversions is essential for clearing the initial aptitude filtering test for campus hiring.

rag_chunks.subject: Aptitude & Interview Prep
rag_chunks.definition: Profit and loss calculations evaluate commercial financial margins relative to original cost basis.
rag_chunks.formula_or_core_rule: CP = SP / (1 + P%). Equivalent discount = D1 + D2 - (D1 * D2 / 100). Dishonest weight gain = Error / (Actual * 100).
rag_chunks.worked_example: Selling at Rs 960 with 20% loss implies CP = 960 / 0.8 = Rs 1200.
rag_chunks.content: Candidates learn rapid problem-solving strategies for multi-tier discounts, marked margins, and false weights.

rag_chunks.subject: Aptitude & Interview Prep
rag_chunks.definition: Time and Work models calculate operational completion schedules using LCM-based task unit efficiencies.
rag_chunks.formula_or_core_rule: Assume Total Work = LCM of given days. Together days = Total Work / Sum of individual daily efficiencies.
rag_chunks.worked_example: A (10d) and B (15d) work on LCM 30 units: 3 + 2 = 5 units/day, completing 30/5 = 6 days.
rag_chunks.content: The LCM technique eliminates fractional additions, cutting solving time significantly during campus selection tests.

rag_chunks.subject: Aptitude & Interview Prep
rag_chunks.definition: Relative speed models the net rate of separation or convergence between two moving bodies.
rag_chunks.formula_or_core_rule: km/h to m/s: multiply 5/18. Avg speed: 2xy/(x+y). Train crosses platform: Distance = L_train + L_platform.
rag_chunks.worked_example: 72 km/h is 20 m/s. Crossing a 300m platform by a 200m train takes (200 + 300) / 20 = 25 seconds.
rag_chunks.content: High-frequency exam questions involve train crossing lengths, opposite/same direction relative speeds, and boat streams.

rag_chunks.subject: Aptitude & Interview Prep
rag_chunks.definition: Number series questions evaluate logical induction by requiring identification of implicit algebraic or geometric patterns.
rag_chunks.formula_or_core_rule: Test differences first. Look for n^2 ± k or n^3 ± n patterns. Check for interleaved dual sequences.
rag_chunks.worked_example: Series 0, 6, 24, 60, 120 corresponds directly to n^3 - n, revealing the next term as 7^3 - 7 = 336.
rag_chunks.content: A staple section of IT placement aptitude tests across Cognizant, Infosys, Capgemini, and TCS.

rag_chunks.subject: Aptitude & Interview Prep
rag_chunks.definition: Blood relations and direction tests evaluate spatial and relational deductive reasoning under time constraints.
rag_chunks.formula_or_core_rule: Draw generational tree (+ for male, - for female). Shortest path = sqrt(dx^2 + dy^2).
rag_chunks.worked_example: A person traveling 6 km West and 8 km North is exactly sqrt(36 + 64) = 10 km North-West of start.
rag_chunks.content: Systematic tree mapping prevents common trap answers in convoluted multi-generation family relation questions.

rag_chunks.subject: Aptitude & Interview Prep
rag_chunks.chapter: Verbal & HR: The STAR Method for Behavioral Interviews
rag_chunks.definition: The STAR framework organizes responses to competency-based behavioral interview questions into a compelling 4-part narrative.
rag_chunks.formula_or_core_rule: Situation (15%) -> Task (15%) -> Action (50%, emphasize 'I') -> Result (20%, quantified metrics).
rag_chunks.worked_example: Structuring a response around a real production outage, detailing profiling actions taken and 40% latency improvement achieved.
rag_chunks.content: Mastering STAR answers gives candidates a significant edge in technical and HR behavioral interviews.

rag_chunks.subject: Aptitude & Interview Prep
rag_chunks.chapter: Verbal & HR: The STAR Method for Behavioral Interviews
rag_chunks.definition: Behavioral evaluations test interpersonal diplomacy, technical trade-off negotiation, and accountability when failures occur.
rag_chunks.formula_or_core_rule: Acknowledge mistakes without deflection, explain corrective technical action, and highlight preventative automated tests built.
rag_chunks.worked_example: Resolving an API contract disagreement with a frontend peer by building a Swagger schema mock specification.
rag_chunks.content: Interviewers at top tech firms (Amazon, Google, Microsoft) heavily index on ownership and growth mindset.

rag_chunks.subject: Aptitude & Interview Prep
rag_chunks.chapter: Technical Resume Building: Action Verbs & Impact Metrics
rag_chunks.definition: The Google XYZ formula structures resume bullets by pairing action verbs and implementation details with quantifiable metrics.
rag_chunks.formula_or_core_rule: 'Accomplished [X] measured by [Y] by doing [Z]'. Use active verbs (Architected, Engineered, Optimized).
rag_chunks.worked_example: 'Engineered Redis caching layer, decreasing 95th-percentile API response latency from 450ms to 65ms across 10k users.'
rag_chunks.content: Crafting high-impact resume bullet points dramatically increases interview call conversion rates during campus placement drives.

rag_chunks.subject: Aptitude & Interview Prep
rag_chunks.chapter: Technical Resume Building: Action Verbs & Impact Metrics
rag_chunks.definition: ATS optimization ensures resume documents parse cleanly through automated hiring scanners with relevant keyword density.
rag_chunks.formula_or_core_rule: Strictly 1 page for freshers, standard single-column hierarchy, live GitHub/demo links, zero typos.
rag_chunks.worked_example: Structuring technical skills into Languages, Frameworks, Databases, and Tools enables immediate ATS keyword indexing.
rag_chunks.content: Guidance on avoiding common student resume pitfalls, fluff descriptors, and multi-page layouts.
